A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the enterprise distributed application performance is a function of the network and computer systems parameters, and the application level performance can be improved by optimizing the network and computer parameters.

we provide a new way of thinking about distributed application performance management, a mathematical model for the allocation of distributed applications and a case study to illustrate the effectiveness of our approach.
the enterprise-wide application level performance can be optimized by allocating application components across LANs, and the BIP model provides a systematic approach to the optimization problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the application-level performance of distributed applications is a function of the network bandwidth and the computer system parameters and that the application-level parameters are also functions of the network bandwidth, the computer system parameters, and the allocation of application components across LANs.
the application-level parameters are not only dependent on the network and computer systems but also on the application components themselves.
the performance of an application running on a DCS is not only dependent on the computer system parameters, but is also dependent on the network performance.
